This Charm must be activated prior to the attack roll.

name: Flitting Shadow Form
summary: Root of the Day Caste Dodge tree; the Exalt channels Essence through his body and movements, making him extremely difficult to strike, reducing the dice pool of a single attack by two dice per mote spent.
description: The Exalt channels Essence through his body and movements, making him extremely difficult to strike. For every mote spent, the Abyssal reduces the dice pool of a single attack roll by two dice. This Charm can only target attacks aimed specifically at the Exalt and may reduce a dice pool to zero (ensuring that the attack misses). Characters may activate this Charm any time after an attack is declared but before dice are rolled. Flitting Shadow Form can only target attacks the Exalt is aware of.

name: Uncanny Impulse Evasion
summary: Whenever a character with this Charm is attacked, she feels a sense of impending dread and may attempt to sidestep an unseen blow on instinct alone, with a dodge pool equal to her unmodified Dexterity.
description: Whenever a character with this Charm is attacked, she feels a sense of impending dread and may attempt to sidestep an unseen blow on instinct alone. The character's dice pool for such a dodge equals her unmodified Dexterity. This Charm cannot be placed in a Combo with other Dodge Charms. If a deathknight's player does not choose to activate this Charm in response to an unseen attack, the Exalt does not sense the blow until it lands. This Charm must be activated prior to the attack roll.

name: Flickering Wisp Technique
summary: The Abyssal ripples and vanishes like smoke in a stiff breeze, coalescing a split second later a short distance away, perfectly dodging any one attack she can perceive without a roll, including magical effects that don't explicitly prohibit dodging.
description: The Abyssal ripples and vanishes like smoke in a stiff breeze, coalescing a split second later a short distance away. This Charm allows the character to perfectly dodge any one attack that he can perceive without a roll, including those without a roll, including those without a roll. The character still cannot dodge magical effects that explicitly prohibit dodging. The character may not move more yards with this technique than his permanent Essence rating and cannot use the Charm to teleport through solid barriers. Flickering Wisp Technique must be activated prior to the attack roll.

name: Flowing Evasion Assault
summary: In addition to teleporting out of harm's way, an Abyssal with this Charm can ensure that she materializes behind her opponent, following the same rules as Flickering Wisp Technique with two extra exceptions, and gaining a free attack from behind.
description: In addition to teleporting out of harm's way, an Abyssal with this Charm can ensure that she materializes behind her opponent. Flowing Evasion Assault follows the same rules as Flickering Wisp Technique with two exceptions. First, the Exalt may reappear as far away as her Dodge in yards. Secondly, if the attacker is within that range, the Abyssal may automatically reappear behind her target. If the Abyssal has any actions remaining to launch an attack of her own, she gains the full benefits of attacking from behind (see Exalted, p. 238).

name: Incomparable Phantom Form
summary: Suffusing his body with spectral Essence, the Abyssal becomes translucent and partially dematerialized, ensuring that he can dodge all incoming attacks, perceived or otherwise, with his full Dexterity + Dodge pool.
description: Suffusing his body with spectral Essence, the Abyssal becomes translucent and partially dematerialized. In addition to unnerving opponents, this transformation allows the Exalt to dodge all incoming attacks, perceived or otherwise, with his full Dexterity + Dodge pool.
prerequisiteText: Uncanny Impulse Evasion; Flickering Wisp Technique

name: Theft of Face
summary: Root of the first Day Caste Larceny branch; by stealing a victim's Essence, a character with this Charm can also steal her visage, becoming her perfect likeness after an hour of meditation.
description: By stealing a victim's Essence, a character with this Charm can also steal her visage. The character must completely drain her victim of blood and spend one hour digesting and studying the stolen Essence. At the conclusion of her meditation, the Exalt shifts into the perfect likeness of her victim. This is not an illusion, but a startling transformation. Every mark and scar is duplicated, and every tic and mannerism compensated for. If questioned, the Exalt can even draw on the stolen memories of her prey with an Intelligence + Larceny roll at a difficulty assigned by the Storyteller. No amount of physical scrutiny can discern that the Abyssal is not whom she pretends to be, although an Abyssal anima victims who are the same gender as the Exalt. Although she may disguise herself as an Exalted victim and even duplicate the powers or anima of an Solar or Lunar scarring, the character cannot emulate the powers or anima of an Exalted victim, but this is not applied. Once the character voluntarily ends this Charm, she loses all memories and shifts back to her true form. Death also ends the ruse. Characters can only assume a given guise once before the memories are digested.

name: Flawless Doppelganger Disguise
summary: This Charm holds the same effects as Theft of Mien, but the disguise persists until the Exalt releases it rather than expiring after an hour.
description: This Charm holds the same effects as Theft of Mien, but the disguise persists until the Exalt releases it rather than expiring automatically.

name: Solar Impersonation Style
summary: By channeling the nascent spark of Solar Essence trapped within her, an Abyssal with this Charm can shift her anima to resemble that of a Chosen of the Unconquered Sun for a day, deceiving all but Zenith Solars or Night Caste with the same technique.
description: By channeling the nascent spark of Solar Essence trapped within her, an Abyssal with this Charm can shift her anima to resemble that of a Chosen of the Unconquered Sun. While this Charm is in effect, the deathknight's anima banner and Caste Mark manifest exactly as a Solar of the appropriate type (Dusk becomes Dawn, Midnight becomes Zenith, etc.). This Charm only affects the anima banner, however. The Exalt retains her true power appropriate to her true Caste. Any Zenith Caste Solar with a Permanent Essence higher than the Abyssal's can see through the disguise. Only Abyssal Exalted may learn this Charm, although it is rumored that some Solars of the Night Caste may have developed a similar technique for impersonating deathknights.

name: Theft of Mien
summary: This Charm duplicates the effects of Theft of Face with one exception: the Exalt also steals intuitive knowledge of her victim's mannerisms and habits, making the ruse much more effective, though close family members can still recognize odd behavior.
description: This Charm duplicates the effects of Theft of Face with one exception: the Exalt also steals intuitive knowledge of her victim's mannerisms and habits. Consequently, the ruse is much more effective and can easily fool casual associates of the target. Close family members can still recognize that something is wrong, regardless of whether they actually suspect an imposter or attribute the odd behavior to illness.

name: Cunning Criminal Style
summary: Root of the second Day Caste Larceny branch; many criminals live short, bleak lives, and an Abyssal who taps into the shared regrets and suffering of the dead has a wealth of information at his disposal about local crime networks.
description: Many criminals live short lives and die just as bleakly. Accordingly, an Abyssal who taps into the shared regrets and suffering of the dead has a wealth of information at his disposal. He can intuitively pick out criminal establishments from honest businesses and discern those who actively desire to sell or buy illegal merchandise. Just as easily, the Abyssal can spot the lines of power in the local crime scene and track them back to the true crime-lords of the area. While this Charm remains active, the character remains at home in any criminal subculture. Cunning Criminal Style cannot discern informers or undercover agents from ordinary criminals unless there are sufficient clues present to draw such a conclusion.

name: Evidence-Erasing Method
summary: With this Charm active, an Abyssal leaves no more evidence of her passing than as she usually would, but she does not drop unintentional clues such as footprints, hair, etc. unless she chooses to.
description: With this Charm active, an Abyssal leaves no more evidence of her passing than she usually would, but she does not drop unintentional clues such as footprints, hair, etc. Obviously, if an Abyssal wants to leave evidence such as physical evidence such as footprints, hair, etc, she may do so, since the Charm only protects against unintentional evidence. Only supernatural tracking can find a character shrouded with this Charm.

name: Lock-Weathering Touch
summary: With this Charm, an Exalt can instantly bypass any mundane lock with a gentle touch; the lock rusts inside with a wisp of acrid smoke, causing the mechanism to fall open.
description: With this Charm, an Exalt can instantly bypass any mundane lock with a gentle touch. The lock rusts inside with a wisp of acrid smoke, causing the mechanism to fall open. This Charm must be used separately on each lock and may affect locked manacles as easily as the bolts of doors or safes.

name: Artful Conjuration Trick
summary: Through the use of this Charm, an Abyssal becomes preternaturally deft at sleight of hand and may perform amazing feats of conjuration and legerdemain without requiring a roll, palming a coin from a pouch or instantly palming a handful of shuriken.
description: Through the use of this Charm, an Abyssal becomes preternaturally deft at sleight of hand and may perform amazing feats of conjuration and legerdemain without requiring a roll. For outright impossible stunts, such as actually summoning a coin from a belt pouch without reaching for it, the Storyteller may require a Dexterity + Larceny roll. This Charm is intended for trickery and bedazzlement, not combat. Instantly palming a handful of shuriken is permissible, but the Charm cannot actually create something from nothing, nor steal possessions from an opponent. The Storyteller retains final say on what can and cannot be done with this Charm.

name: Concealing Distraction Discipline
summary: Root of the Day Caste Stealth tree; briefly eroding the attention span of onlookers with a gentle rush of Essence, an Abyssal with this Charm becomes far more difficult to notice until she draws attention or is spotted.
description: Briefly eroding the attention span of onlookers with a gentle rush of Essence, an Abyssal with this Charm becomes far more difficult to notice. Until the end of the scene, all attempts to spot the Exalt increase their difficulty by his permanent Essence. This increase applies only so long as the Abyssal does not draw undue attention to himself and remains unnoticed. If he is spotted by anyone, the Charm immediately ends and cannot be reactivated until the Exalt moves entirely out of sight.

name: Encounter-Banishing Gesture
summary: Despite their prowess, even the most stealthy and nimble Day Castes get caught from time to time; with this Charm, a character can rip the memory of an encounter from a target's mind so that he forgets he ever saw the Exalt.
description: Despite their prowess, even the most stealthy and nimble Day Castes get caught from time to time. With this Charm, a character can rip the memory of an encounter from a target's mind so that he forgets he ever saw the Exalt. The Abyssal's player rolls Manipulation + Stealth against a difficulty of the target's Essence (or highest Essence in the case of a group). For every success rolled, the target forgets the events of that turn. Thus, four successes erase the past four turns of a target's memory. As an added benefit, a befuddled target will not notice the Abyssal again for a like number of turns unless she draws attention to herself again for a while longer. This gives the Exalt a few seconds to escape and conceal herself more thoroughly. This Charm has no effect on beings with a higher permanent Essence than the Abyssal or against beings who are physically agitated (for example, those in combat).

name: Splinter in the Mind's Eye
summary: This Charm duplicates the effects and rules of Encounter-Banishing Gesture, except that its effects extend to a number of witnesses equal to the Abyssal's Essence rating x 10 without requiring more motes for each observer.
description: This Charm duplicates the effects and rules of Encounter-Banishing Gesture, except that its effects extend to a number of witnesses equal to the Abyssal's Essence rating x 10 without requiring more motes for each observer.

name: Noiseless Phantom Style
summary: Enveloped in the stillness of the grave, an Abyssal with this Charm makes no noise -- her footsteps do not echo or splash, and she can jump or stomp in perfect eerie silence, though her voice and magic still work normally.
description: Enveloped in the stillness of the grave, an Abyssal with this Charm makes no noise. Her footsteps do not echo or splash, and she can jump or stomp in perfect eerie silence. Conversely, she cannot speak or employ any magic that relies on sound. This Charm only works against sounds made by the character, however. Her blade might slice soundlessly through a victim's ribs, but the effect would not muffle the victim's scream of pain or rasping death rattle.

name: Shadow Cloak Technique
summary: The Abyssal cocoons himself in pure darkness, taking on the wraithlike appearance of a solidified shadow; so long as he remains in darkness or among other shadows, he adds 1 die per 2 motes spent to all Stealth rolls.
description: The Abyssal cocoons himself in pure darkness, taking on the wraithlike appearance of a solidified shadow. So long as he remains in darkness or among other shadows, he adds 1 die per 2 motes spent to all Stealth rolls. The Exalt cannot purchase more dice with this Charm than twice his Essence rating. If a bright light is shined on the hidden Exalt, his cloak dissolves immediately, and the Charm ends.

name: Stifled Cry Exercise
summary: The Abyssal focuses on a single victim within line of sight and smothers his voice with Essence; until the end of the turn the target cannot speak or make any other vocalized noise, useful for Day Caste assassins to prevent victims from screaming.
description: The character focuses on a single victim within line of sight and smothers his voice with Essence. Until the end of the turn, the target cannot speak or make any other vocalized noise. Day Caste assassins often employ this Charm to prevent their victims from screaming. This Charm has no effect on beings with a higher permanent Essence than the Abyssal.

name: Unseen Wisp Method
summary: The Abyssal vanishes wholly from sight, dissolving in a ripple of scattering shadows; ranged attacks against her are all but impossible without magical aid or well-directed stunts.
description: The Abyssal vanishes wholly from sight, dissolving in a ripple of scattering shadows. For a number of turns equal to half the number of motes invested, the Exalt is nothing more than a wavering blur in the air. Ranged attacks against her are all but impossible without magical aid or well-directed stunts, while close-range attacks suffer a difficulty penalty of the deathknight's permanent Essence.

name: Argument-Slaying Remark
summary: By speaking brusquely and projecting an aura of menace, an Abyssal with this Charm can cut through the drawn-out process of debate, ending an argument within moments with the best resolution the target could have achieved through continued discussion.
description: By speaking brusquely and projecting an aura of menace, an Abyssal with this Charm can cut through the drawn-out process of debate. The targeted argument ends within moments with the best resolution the target could have achieved with continued discussion. For example, a character could use this Charm to derive the best price from a merchant, saving minutes or perhaps even hours of haggling. Note that Argument-Slaying Remark isn't a perfect 'final word' Charm -- if an answer would be no regardless of what the Abyssal might say or argue, then the answer remains no. This Charm simply brings the matter to a conclusion instantly.

name: Authority-Eroding Technique
summary: Root of one Moonshadow Caste Bureaucracy branch; through this Charm, an Abyssal can momentarily confuse a target and weaken her effectiveness in a critical moment, reducing her dice pool for a single Bureaucracy roll.
description: Through this Charm, an Abyssal can momentarily confuse a target and weaken her effectiveness in a critical moment. For every mote spent, the target loses one die from a single Bureaucracy roll. This Charm cannot reduce a victim's dice pool lower than her Essence. Authority-Eroding Technique may be invoked any time after an appropriate action is declared but before dice are rolled. The Abyssal can even set up the targeted roll, as by asking a pointed question in a meeting.

name: Corruption-Sensing Scrutiny
summary: Root of the second Moonshadow Caste Bureaucracy branch; with this Charm, an Abyssal can perceive corrupt officials and bureaucrats by a distinctive oily stain on their aura, or intuitively gauge a clean official's susceptibility to corruption.
description: With this Charm, an Abyssal can perceive corrupt officials and bureaucrats by a distinctive oily stain on their aura. Alternately, she can intuitively gauge a 'clean' official's susceptibility to corruption. Her player rolls Perception + Bureaucracy against a difficulty of the target's Essence score. The amount of information gleaned depends on the number of successes rolled. Simple success allows the Abyssal to sense whether the target has ever engaged in corruption or not (i.e., accepted a bribe, doctored a report, etc.). With three successes, the character can measure the depth of a target's corruption or her overall vulnerability to such. Thus, she can distinguish the minor blotches of a plagiarizing poet who secretly assassinated his rivals. With five successes, the Abyssal gains a vague sense of the target's offenses, though without the context or specifics. This hunch enables the deathknight to take advantage of a hidden official's weakness or vice -- or simply to know whom best to bribe.

name: Alluring Eloquence Method
summary: This Charm allows an Exalt to vocalize a course of action or point of view with such eloquence and grace that opponents find it difficult or even impossible to argue, resisted by a Bureaucracy or Performance roll augmented with the deathknight's Essence rating.
description: This Charm allows an Exalt to vocalize a course of action or point of view with such eloquence and grace that opponents find it difficult or even impossible to argue. The Abyssal's player makes the Bureaucracy or Performance roll as normal, but all rivals add the deathknight's Essence rating to their countarguments.

name: Cunning Subversion Style
summary: With a few artfully placed rumors and whispers, an Abyssal with this Charm can sow the seeds of discord and mistrust within a particular bureau or organization, causing it to grind to a halt and factionalism.
description: With a few artfully placed rumors and whispers, an Abyssal with this Charm can sow the seeds of discord and mistrust within a particular bureau or organization. Tempers flare, growing mistrust leads to outright hostility and factionalism; the bureau steadily grinds to a halt and implodes under the weight of indolence and excess. This Charm can fully affect a department whose total membership is no greater than the deathknight's Essence rating x 20. If the character wishes to affect a larger organization, he must use this Charm multiple times or settle for a slower, less effect one at random. Regardless, it takes time for infighting and paranoia to build to an extent that it actually impedes efficiency. While this is left to Storytellers to adjudicate, the overall corruption and rivalry effect plays a significant role, as does the quality and strength of leadership within the organization. Generally, this Charm is beyond the scope of rules and has little tangible effect. Its intangible effects can be quite dramatic, however. Few organizations with mortal total members can withstand more than a month of this Charm without utterly disintegrating.

name: Iron Tyrant Mien
summary: Exuding menace and prowess in equal measure, an Abyssal can enchant his authority to sow fear and discourage rebellion; while active, individuals with a Willpower rating lower than the character's cannot organize rebellion against him.
description: Exuding menace and prowess in equal measure, an Abyssal can enchant his authority to sow fear and discourage rebellion. The character must have some recognized leadership position in order to use this Charm, although the type and scope of leadership doesn't matter. A caravan master can surpass a king in brutal tyranny. While this Charm is active, no one with a Willpower score lower than the character's Essence rating may act against the deathknight's authority, let alone participate in outright rebellion. Individuals with a Willpower rating equal to the character's Willpower may act against the despot, but her players suffer a difficulty increase of the character's permanent Essence on all Social rolls to rally others to the cause. Characters whose Willpower exceeds the Abyssal's are, as always, immune to this Charm, as are all magical beings. Also, this Charm only affects members of the hierarchy over which the Exalt presides. A great monarch could order any subject about but would have no authority over a foreign citizen. Storyteller discretion is particularly important in preventing abuse of this Charm. Of course, a large sphere of influence carries its own risks. Besides the likelihood that a strong-willed champion will organize a coup, corrupt tyrants also attract jealous rivals who wish to usurp their power.

name: Regime-Toppling Insinuation
summary: This Charm closely parallels Cunning Subversion Style, but rather than targeting an organization, the Abyssal focuses her havoc against a specific leader, making his orders morose or disregarded by subordinates.
description: This Charm closely parallels Cunning Subversion Style, however, the Abyssal may focus the havoc against a specific leader. If there is no actual coup or assassination attempt -- though there might be -- the concomitant treachery and distrust makes all but the most tyrannical control ineffective. The victim's orders are twisted or disregarded by subordinates, while overall morale drops to an all-time low. Each application of this Charm may permanently affect a number of people equal to the character's Essence rating x 20. As with Cunning Subversion Style, this Charm is primarily a matter of roleplaying rather than rules. Still, it is unlikely that any mortal leader can last more than a month with a hierarchy under his control full of hatred and mistrust toward him. Whether he is pushed out of office or stabbed to death in an alley depends very much on the nature of the victim's subordinates and the type of organization. Ironically, true tyrants have little to fear from negative popular opinion, as they already know how to retain authority in the face of a widespread hierarchy.

name: Language Absorbing Method
summary: Root of one Moonshadow Caste Linguistics branch; with this Charm, an Abyssal may absorb a victim's knowledge of language even as he devours her Essence, so that the deathknight speaks the tongue with perfect fluency and no trace of accent.
description: With this Charm, an Abyssal may absorb a victim's knowledge of language even as he devours her Essence. The character must have consumed at least 1 mote from the target sometime during the scene -- whether through blood drinking, Charms, etc. His player rolls Wits + Linguistics, with a difficulty of (5 - the total number of motes taken). If this lowers the difficulty below 0, no roll is needed. If the roll succeeds, the Abyssal instantly knows one language of his choice known to the target. This knowledge is absolute -- the deathknight speaks with perfect fluency and no trace of accent and may read and write in the tongue so long as the target knew how to do so. If the character consumes more than 5 motes, he may spend double the requisite experience point to digest his stolen linguistics knowledge and permanently increase his Linguistics rating on the spot. Otherwise, languages absorbed with this Charm fade completely when the Charm expires.

name: Confusion of Tongues
summary: Cursing sharply in the lost tongue of the Malfeans, the Abyssal distorts all communication in a zone around her; no one inside this area of effect can understand written or spoken language.
description: Cursing sharply in the lost tongue of the Malfeans, the Abyssal distorts all communication in a zone around her. No one inside this area of effect can understand written or spoken language. Familiar letters run together into baffling glyphs, while every spoken phrase twists into complete gibberish. Clever characters can still communicate simple concepts via pantomime or crude drawings, but formal or established hand signs convey no more meaning than any spoken tongue. The character makes a Manipulation + Linguistics roll against the targets, with a difficulty equal to the targets' highest permanent Essence. This Charm has no effect on beings whose permanent Essence matches or exceeds the Abyssal's. However, while such beings hear and see languages as they truly are, their own words remain twisted to affected beings. The zone of distortion extends to a radius of (the character's permanent Essence x 3) yards. With vocalized speech, neither party projects information as they truly intend to convey. This Charm does not allow deeper mind reading or memory probing, nor does it preclude deception.

name: Peerless Fluency Style
summary: As the warrior-poets of the Underworld, many Abyssal Exalted speak and write with haunting skill and eloquence; for every mote spent, the character may add one die to all Linguistics rolls for a specific known language.
description: As the warrior-poets of the Underworld, many Abyssal Exalted speak and write with haunting skill and eloquence. For every mote spent on this Charm, the character may add one die to all Linguistics rolls for a specific known language. These dice are mechanically identical to a Linguistics specialty (see Exalted, p. 140) and may similarly add to other communication-related rolls, at Storyteller discretion. The character cannot purchase more bonus dice for any language than her Intelligence score. Note that characters with four or more dice of fluency convey superhuman grace, is immediately evident to any listener or reader. Indeed, slow-witted mortals may have trouble following the cadence and intricate vocabulary of such characters.

name: Theft of Words
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal can temporarily excise a victim's comprehension of a particular language, indicating a target within line of sight and whispering softly to strip their understanding.
description: With this Charm, an Abyssal can temporarily excise a victim's comprehension of a particular language. The Exalt whispers softly in the maddening dialect of the Malfeans and indicates a target within line of sight. His player then rolls Manipulation + Linguistics against a difficulty of the target's permanent Essence. For every success rolled, the character may spend 5 motes to remove a random language or pick a language known by the Abyssal and suppress it. The latter is a gamble, however, unless the Exalt is certain his target knows the language in question. Individuals deprived of all languages cannot speak or write at all, although they may attempt to grunt and crudely pantomime their intentions. Once the duration ends, the target regains full memory of all her forgotten languages. This Charm has no effect on beings with a higher permanent Essence than the Exalt.

name: Words Beneath a Whisper
summary: An Abyssal with this Charm may communicate telepathically with anyone she knows to invoke this Charm, projecting thoughts at will as a reflexive action to speak with someone she does not share a language with.
description: An Abyssal with this Charm may communicate entirely telepathically with anyone she knows to invoke this Charm. The character must be able to directly sense her target to invoke this Charm. If at any time the Exalt cannot perceive her target, the connection instantly breaks, and the Charm ends. While the link remains, the Abyssal can project her thoughts at will as a reflexive action, enabling her to speak with someone she does not share a language with. The target knows the thoughts come from outside his mind, although he cannot pinpoint their source without other magic unless the Exalt identifies herself. Similarly, the target may project his own thoughts and replies along the link. As with vocalized speech, neither party projects information they do not intend to convey. This Charm does not allow deeper mind reading or memory probing, nor does it preclude deception.

name: Blood Inscription Technique
summary: Root of the second Moonshadow Caste Linguistics branch; by channeling Essence-laden blood through his fingertips, an Exalt with this Charm knows his writing always makes marks resembling tattoos that gradually fade over days or weeks like applied dye.
description: By channeling Essence-laden blood through his fingertips, an Exalt with this Charm knows his writing always leaves marks. As the Abyssal traces glyphs with his fingers, his touch leaves marks of indelible crimson. Marks etched with this Charm are virtually indistinguishable from ink stains and can be cleaned or removed as if the writing surface permits. If used to mark living beings, the glyphs resemble tattoos, but gradually fade over a period of days or weeks like any applied dye. Characters using this Charm write with uncanny precision, easily matching the graceful calligraphy of even a very fine stylus or brush.

name: Ghost-Warding Glyph
summary: By tracing a mystical rune on a target's forehead, an Abyssal with this Charm may protect an individual from hungry ghosts and walking dead; the mark washes off after a day, and the Abyssal may use the Glyph on himself.
description: By tracing a mystical rune on a target's forehead, an Abyssal with this Charm may protect an individual from hungry ghosts and walking dead. The mark washes off and retains a slick appearance until after it dries. For the duration of the Charm, no zombie or bestial ghost will attack the target unless compelled to do so by a necromancer, an Abyssal, or some other supernatural compulsion. Sentient ghosts generally leave the character alone out of fear of the Deathlords but are not compelled to. This Charm has no effect on Exalted, but any display of an anima banner or Caste Mark burns off the rune and revokes the protection. The Abyssal may use the Ghost-Warding Glyph on himself.

name: Glyph-Unveiling Meditation
summary: By touching a sample of writing, an Abyssal with this Charm can attune his mind to the lingering wisps of memory left by the author, reading the tainted work with perfect fluency and comprehension.
description: By touching a sample of writing, an Abyssal with this Charm can attune his mind to the lingering wisps of memory left by the author. The Exalt can read the targeted work with perfect fluency, but loses attunement or comprehension as soon as he stops reading or reaches the end of the document. Note that it is not necessary to read in a linear manner; he may skim passages, jump ahead and reread sections as many times as desired. However, once the Abyssal halts to pursue another task, the Charm ends. Although an Exalt can quote specific passages or recall exact wording after the Charm ends, he will still remember what he read and what it meant. This Charm does not work against artificial languages, codes and other such methods of deliberately obscuring the content of a work, as the author's intent is devious and the traces left behind are opaque.

name: Scathing Cynic Attitude
summary: A character using this Charm becomes preternaturally resistant to all forms of persuasion, from simple argument to outright mind control; her Nature changes to Critic for the duration.
description: A character using this Charm becomes preternaturally resistant to all forms of persuasion, from simple argument to outright mind control. For the duration of the Charm, the character's Nature changes to Critic. Any time the deathknight is subjected to words of magic that would alter his point of view or perceptions, his player may reflexively roll Willpower against a difficulty equal to the offending character's Essence. Success allows the Abyssal to scornfully shrug off the suggestion. Characters using this Charm are notably brusque and bitter, which adds +1 to the difficulty of all Charisma rolls. Scathing Cynic Attitude cannot defend against persuasion by beings with a higher permanent Essence than the character's Willpower.
prerequisiteText: Peerless Fluency Style; Blood Inscription Technique

name: Soul Reins
summary: Root of the Moonshadow Caste Ride tree; a character with this Charm can subdue a mount with her supernatural will, reducing its Control Rating for every mote spent.
description: A character with this Charm can subdue a mount with her supernatural will. For every mote spent, the targeted animal has its Control Rating reduced by one point. If this reduces the steed's Control Rating to zero, it obeys unhesitatingly and will jump to its death if so directed. Mounts tamed with this Charm only obey the Exalt. All other characters must contend with the beast's normal Control Rating. Soul Reins only affects animals trained for riding -- characters cannot jump on the back of a wild tyrant lizard and expect compliance.

name: Mount-Breaking Method
summary: Similar to Soul Reins, this Charm allows an Exalt to dominate a steed and subsume its will to her own, permanently reducing the mount's Control Rating and granting immunity to terror when ridden by the Abyssal.
description: Similar to Soul Reins, this Charm allows a deathknight to dominate a steed and subsume its will to her own. Unlike the lesser Charm, however, the effects of Mount-Breaking Method are permanent. The character's player rolls Strength + Ride against a difficulty of the animal's Control Rating. Each success permanently reduces the mount's Control Rating by one point, to a minimum score of one. If the Abyssal's player actually rolls enough successes to reduce a Control Rating to zero, the beast gains immunity to terror when ridden by the Exalt. Although the final outcome is a foregone conclusion based on the results of the roll, the character must still spend the rest of the scene aggressively taming her steed. Unless this roll is botched, the Exalt will not suffer injury during the training session. The Charm actually weakens the core of the beast rather than simply compelling obedience, so the mount's new Control Rating applies to all riders. Mount-Breaking Method may affect any animal that can possibly be trained to accept a rider, even dangerous beasts such as hydroc or bear. The character must have a permanent Essence of 3 or higher to train exotic or deadly animals, however.

name: Tireless Charger Technique
summary: With this Charm, a mounted character can briefly sustain and push his steed with raw Essence, granting boundless energy at the cost of unsoakable lethal damage to the mount each hour it's maintained.
description: With this Charm, a mounted character can briefly sustain and push his steed with raw Essence. Tireless Charger Technique lasts until the Abyssal dismounts or a number of hours have passed equal to his Ride score. Enchanted steeds have boundless energy and never need to stop for food or water. The necrotic Essence powering this Charm also eats at the animal's life force. For every hour or fraction thereof that the Charm is maintained, the horse suffers one level of unsoakable lethal damage. This damage is deferred until the Charm ends. After a horse suffers from this Charm, it cannot be safely re-enchanted with this Charm until it fully heals its wounds. Doing otherwise allows the horse to act at full strength again, but immediately kills the mount when the forced march ends.

name: Forceful Spirit Spur
summary: An Abyssal with this Charm can silently summon her mount from great distances; the steed feels the bite of phantom spurs digging harshly into its flanks unless it moves at best possible speed toward the Exalt.
description: An Abyssal with this Charm can silently summon her mount from great distances. The steed feels the bite of phantom spurs digging harshly into her flanks unless it moves at best possible speed toward the Exalt. This Charm has a range of (the character's permanent Essence x 10) miles. The Abyssal must have clearly exerted dominance over the summoned animal before it will answer a summons. Such dominance can have been achieved through physical (such as beating or through rough use of a whip) or mystical (as in the case of Soul Reins) means. While animals under the influence of this Charm are distracted or become lost, they cannot circumvent complex obstacles any better than normal. The compulsion inflicted by this Charm remains in force until the animal reaches its master or moves beyond range.

name: Mount-Spooking Shout
summary: The Abyssal pours Essence into his voice, unleashing an unholy shriek that terrifies most steeds; all living mounts within earshot must make a roll or rear and bolt unless pushed for short agonizing bursts by their rider.
description: The Abyssal pours Essence into his voice, unleashing an unholy shriek that terrifies most steeds. All living mounts within earshot of the character rear and bolt unless the players of their riders or team drivers makes a successful Charisma + Ride roll against a difficulty of the shouting Abyssal's Essence. Even if this roll succeeds, affected mounts remain skittish and add one to their Control Rating for the rest of the scene. This increase is cumulative if the Abyssal emits more than one such scream in a scene. Mount-Spooking Shout does not terrify the Abyssal's own steed, nor does the Charm have any effect on beasts other than pack animals or actual mounts.

name: Spectral Steed
summary: With this Charm, a character may summon a ghost horse from the Essence of the Underworld, materializing out of dusky smoke with the statistics of a war horse but tireless, fearless, and biting with an inflicted 4L bite.
description: With this Charm, a character may summon a ghost horse from the Essence of the Underworld. Materializing out of dusky smoke, the beast has the appearance of a pure black stallion with eyes like smoldering coals and sharp teeth no horse alive should have. It has the same statistics as a war horse of excellent quality (see Exalted, p. 316), but it is utterly tireless, fearless and inflicts 4L with a successful bite. Spectral steeds do not need food or drink, but enjoy the taste of human flesh and blood. If a character drains this Charm again after its duration expires, a new horse appears, and the old one dissolves with a screaming whinny.

name: Foundering Foal Gesture
summary: Gesturing sharply at a mount in her line of sight, the Abyssal curses her target with weakness and pain; the steed cannot move any faster than a walk unless pushed for short agonizing bursts by its rider.
description: Gesturing sharply at a mount in her line of sight, the Abyssal curses her target with weakness and pain. The steed cannot move any faster than a walk unless pushed for short agonizing bursts by its rider. Foundering Foal Gesture can affect multiple animals at a cost of 4 motes each. As with Mount-Spooking Shout, this Charm only affects pack animals and steeds, although magical beasts and those strengthened with magic are also immune.

name: Master Sailor's Memory
summary: Root of the Moonshadow Caste Sail tree; the character momentarily closes his eyes and dredges memories from the drowned dead of the Underworld, intuitively understanding the craft of sailing as if from decades of experience at sea.
description: The character momentarily closes his eyes and dredges memories from the drowned dead of the Underworld. When he opens his eyes, he intuitively understands the craft of sailing as though from decades of experience at sea.

name: Crew Sustaining Technique
summary: Channeling the Essence of the Underworld and his own life force, the character can reduce a crew's need for food and rest; the character must spend one Willpower, plus 1 mote for every crewmember she wishes to enchant.
description: Channeling the Essence of the Underworld and his own life force, the character may reduce a crew's need for food and rest. The character must spend one Willpower, plus 1 mote for every crewmember she wishes to enchant, thereafter the sailors' life energy is absorbed powering the Charm, reducing the cost to 1 mote per sailor per week. As a side effect, characters steadily kill off pests or vermin aboard the ship. If there are rats or other vermin aboard, their life energy is absorbed powering the Charm, reducing the cost to 1 mote per sailor per week. This side effect steadily kills off pests or vermin aboard the ship, and after two or three applications most sailors regard as a good omen. Unless a ship is very large or very infested, it takes only one or two applications of this Charm to completely eradicate all vermin aboard. A sailor enscorcelled with Crew Sustaining Technique needs about a quarter of the food, water and rest that he normally does. She does not suffer from scurvy or other dietary deficiencies from substandard rations and long unusually enervated. Long-term exposure is dangerous, however. If this Charm is used on a character for more days than her Stamina score, each successive day reduces her Stamina by one dot. Characters reduced to zero Stamina die at the rate of one point per day. Only after a character has fully recovered her Stamina can she be safely enchanted again. This Charm has no effect on beings whose statistics are otherwise superhuman.

name: Ghost Wind Prana
summary: The Abyssal stands on deck, arms upraised and crackling with Essence as she summons a cold wind from the Underworld which exists to propel her vessel and displaces all natural breezes for that purpose.
description: The Abyssal stands on deck, arms upraised and crackling with Essence, as she summons a cold wind from the Underworld. This wind only exists to propel her vessel and displaces all natural breezes for that purpose, but otherwise, it does not disturb the water or wind for other vessels (though they may hear its eerie howling). Ships so enchanted move as though their sails were full in their rigging, regardless of the prevailing wind's direction or the course set by the helmsman. The spectral wind never gets deflected; ships sailing in a hurricane must still contend with the dangers of such a gale.

name: Ghost on the Deck
summary: The Exalt adds one to his Sail rating for every mote spent, cannot raise a character's Sail above 5, and never botches balance rolls while using this Charm; the rest of the crew fly overboard from a hit but the deathknight stands unruffled.
description: The Exalt adds one dot to his Sail rating for every mote spent, although this Charm cannot raise a character's Sail above 5. In addition, Exalted using this Charm never botch a roll to keep their balance in tumultuous seas, but they can still fall normally. This Charm digs deeper into the memories of sailors long dead, allowing the character to guide his every movement. While this Charm is in effect, the character can perfectly balance and stride effortlessly across the deck or scurry up rigging without requiring a roll, even in the middle of a howling typhoon or on impact with a submerged reef. The rest of the crew may fly overboard from the impact or lashing waves, but the Exalt stands entirely unruffled. Characters using this Charm are also completely immune to seasickness.

name: Hull-Hardening Technique
summary: By laying hands against a hull and willing Essence to flow through its timbers, an Abyssal with this Charm can mystically reinforce her vessel; the ship gains 1L of soak per mote spent, purchasable multiple times.
description: By laying hands against a hull and willing Essence to flow through its timbers, an Abyssal with this Charm can mystically reinforce her vessel. The ship gains 1L of soak per mote spent, although the deathknight cannot purchase more points of soak than her Stamina + Sail. This limit applies to all applications of the Charm in a scene. Hull-Hardening Technique does not require Willpower if used for another application while the Charm remains active. Hulls regularly treated with this Charm look bleached and weathered before their time, although they retain the durability of their true age.
cost: 1 mote per L of soak, plus 1 Willpower

name: Phantom Sail Technique
summary: With this Charm, a character channels Essence to patch the rips and tears of a damaged sail; for the next 24 hours the sail behaves as if undamaged and provides appropriate propulsion.
description: With this Charm, a character channels Essence to patch the rips and tears of a damaged sail and rigging. The character concentrates and raises his hand, summoning a morass of shadows to spread over the targeted sail. For the next 24 hours, the sail behaves as if undamaged and provides appropriate propulsion. If a ship has multiple sails, the Exalt may have to use this Charm more than once. While Phantom Sail Technique can restore clinging tatters to full function, it cannot create a sail from nothing. At least some identifiable vestiges must remain.

name: Wind-Killing Stance
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal can extend a zone of stillness from him, displacing even the fiercest gales with its periphery; the Exalt stands on deck and traces a horizontal arc, creating a sphere of calm.
description: With this Charm, an Abyssal can extend a zone of stillness from him, displacing even the fiercest gales with its periphery. The Exalt stands on deck and concentrates, tracing a horizontal arc with his arms. At the conclusion of the gesture, a spherical wave of Essence flashes out to the arc to a radius of (the character's permanent Essence x 15) yards. This artificial stillness moves with the Exalt and lasts for one scene or until his creator dies or moves more than a yard from his original location on deck. The character can still speak and gesture normally while maintaining Wind-Killing Stance, however. Wind-Killing Stance cannot stop magical storms or breezes created by magical beings unless the deathknight's Essence substantially less powerful (Storyteller's discretion). This Charm is primarily to weather storms and to prevent enemy sailing vessels from escaping.
prerequisiteText: Ghost on the Deck; Ghost Wind Prana

name: Hull-Restoring Meditation
summary: The Abyssal extends his anima through the hull, caulking and patching breaches and split seams with raw Essence; the amount of Essence spent to repair damage scales with the ship's damage and size.
description: The Abyssal extends his anima through the hull, caulking and patching breaches and split seams with raw Essence. This energy calcifies into a durable material with the consistency and appearance of bleached bone. Repairing combat damage requires the Abyssal to spend motes equal to the ship's destroyed or damaged rating, as appropriate to the severity of the damage. For non-combat repairs and general caulking, the Storyteller should assign an Essence cost based on the severity of the damage and the ship's size. Sealing a leaky warship requires considerably more Essence than a river yacht. While this Charm can stave off certain destruction by sealing massive breaches, it does not remove handling penalties for water trapped in the hull. Such penalties remain until the water is pumped or bailed out normally.

name: Unsinkable Derelict Preservation
summary: Although it is possible to strengthen and repair ships with lesser Charms, an Abyssal with Unsinkable Derelict Preservation can enchant a ship to ignore damage entirely for one day, keeping out water and moving with its normal maneuverability and speed.
description: Although it is possible to strengthen and repair ships with lesser Charms, an Abyssal with Unsinkable Derelict Preservation can enchant a ship to ignore damage entirely. The Exalt channels Essence through the ship's hull, temporarily sealing all breaks and gashes with translucent wisps of relic from the Underworld. Ships enscorcelled with this Charm act entirely as if whole, keeping out water and moving with their normal maneuverability and speed. Further damage is also similarly ignored for the Charm's duration. Once the Charm's protection ends, severely damaged vessels take on water and sink normally. This Charm can even restore a rotting hulk to full operation, so long as enough of the ship's remains identify the ship. Vessels that have broken asunder cannot be enchanted; they lack the material foundation to accept relic grafts. Ultimately, the Storyteller is the final arbiter of whether or not a ship retains enough substance to preserve. This Charm can affect First Age designs.

name: Exquisite Etiquette Style
summary: Root of the Moonshadow Caste Socialize tree; the Abyssal attunes his mind to the communal memories of the dead to act with faultless (if not officious) propriety and decorum.
description: The Abyssal attunes his mind to the communal memories of the dead to act with faultless propriety and decorum. Characters under the effects of this Charm become faultlessly -- but not officiously -- polite. They instinctively know the appropriate greeting customs or table manners for their situation and never run the risk of making an unintentional faux pas. This Charm is paramount importance when dealing with ancient ghosts whose cultures and customs have long since fallen to the passing of Ages.

name: Heart-Hardening Method
summary: By infecting a target's very soul with festering Essence, the Abyssal can sow doubt in the importance of a particular Virtue, temporarily or permanently reducing a rating via a Manipulation + Socialize roll.
description: By infecting a target's very soul with festering Essence, the Abyssal can sow doubt on the importance of a particular Virtue, casting doubt on the target. The Exalt must spend several minutes talking to the target, casting doubt on the importance of a particular Virtue; her player then rolls Manipulation + Socialize, with a difficulty equal to the targeted Virtue. The victim temporarily loses one dot of the appropriate Virtue for every success in excess of its rating. If the number of successes exceed the target's Willpower score, the target also loses a permanent dot of the Virtue. Whether temporary or permanent, this Charm cannot reduce a Virtue below a rating of one. Virtues that are temporarily diminished return at the rate of one dot per hour. The Abyssal can even use this Charm on herself, with appropriate successes detracting from the targeted Virtue as normal. While this rationalization process has its uses -- particularly in situations when scruples are a liability -- the Abyssal risks permanent Virtue loss if she rationalizes too well. Although a victim ensorcelled by this Charm retains his Nature, his behavior reflects his new Virtue rating. A Thrillseeker deprived of his once-considerable Valor will be torn by desires and a curiosity he can no longer bring himself to express. Likewise, a Survivor dropped to Compassion 1 will do practically anything to anyone in order to preserve his existence.

name: Imprecation of Ill Manners
summary: The Abyssal concentrates on a victim in his line of sight, silently projecting a surge of visceral anger into her subconscious; for the rest of the turn, the target loses one die from all Socialize dice pools for every mote spent.
description: The Abyssal concentrates on a victim in his line of sight, silently projecting a surge of visceral anger into her subconscious. For the rest of the turn, the target loses one die from all Socialize dice pools for every mote spent. This reduction manifests as poor manners, Freudian slips and other, similar gaffes. It is impossible to determine that the Charm's target is acting under the influence of a curse or similar magical means, although astute observers (Perception + Awareness 4+) may suspect that something is amiss.

name: Loyalty Withering Technique
summary: Caressing a victim's mind with the corrupting taint of the Void, an Abyssal with this Charm can plant seeds of doubt in the faithful and erode trust in favor of treachery, temporarily eroding a Virtue by a number of successes.
description: Caressing a victim's mind with the corrupting taint of the Void, an Abyssal with this Charm can plant seeds of doubt in the faithful and erode trust in favor of treachery. The character need only spend a few minutes talking to her target; her player then rolls Manipulation + Socialize against a difficulty chosen by the Storyteller. This difficulty reflects the overall devotion of the target to the selected individual or cause. If she rolls enough successes, the target becomes suspicious and hostile toward whomever or whatever the Abyssal desires. This treacherous dislike lasts a number of hours equal to the deathknight's permanent Essence. If the Exalt receives more successes than necessary, this duration is measured in days rather than hours. This Charm has no effect on beings with a higher Essence rating than the Abyssal.

name: Sin-Sensing Meditation
summary: As cynical as they are pragmatic, characters with this Charm recognize that everyone can be bought; their price might be jade or jewels, a secret vice instead -- but regardless, there is always something a person cannot resist or refuse.
description: As cynical as they are pragmatic, characters with this Charm recognize that everyone can be bought. Their price might be jade or jewels, a secret vice instead -- but regardless, there is always something a person cannot resist or refuse. To have the object of her desire, an Abyssal knows precisely what that object is for her target. He may not have the means of satisfying the desire in question, particularly if it is nigh impossible to acquire, but at least, he knows. The Storyteller should consider the nature of a target's weakness, keeping in mind the target's Nature and Temperance score. Low Temperance characters are less disciplined and, thus, have easier wants to satisfy. High Temperance characters are invariably more difficult and complicated to satiate. It is always possible that some beatific saint exists on whom this Charm would have no effect, but no deathknight has ever met such a person in the decadent Age of Sorrows.

name: Intimations of Mortality
summary: Some Abyssal Exalted are particularly adept at seeding the minds of mortals with doubts about the true nature of life and death that they come to be obsessed with their own mortality, becoming depressed and withdrawn if the roll succeeds.
description: Some Abyssal Exalted are particularly adept at seeding the minds of mortals with such doubts about the true nature of life and death that they come to be obsessed with their own mortality. A deathknight must speak with a target at least briefly (the exchange need only be a few sentences), and the Abyssal's player then makes a Manipulation + Socialize roll with a difficulty of the target's permanent Essence. If successful, the target becomes depressed and withdrawn, suffering a +2 difficulty to all Social rolls for the next 24 hours. If this Charm is used continuously on an unExalted target for more than days than her Conviction rating, her depression blossoms into an actual derangement. Targets afflicted this way continue to suffer Social penalties even after the Charm wears off.

name: Passion-Unveiling Glance
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal perceives the flickering aura of emotion and passion overlaying her target, gleaning the target's most surface feelings or, with more successes, a full sense of currently felt emotions and Virtue/Willpower allocation.
description: With this Charm, an Abyssal perceives the flickering aura of emotion and passion overlaying her target. The Abyssal's player rolls Perception + Socialize against standard difficulty if the target is not trying to conceal or misrepresent his feelings. Otherwise, the target's player reflexively rolls Manipulation + Performance to resist. The amount of information the Abyssal gleans depends on the number of successes rolled beyond what the target may have garnered. Simple success reveals the target's most surface feelings, and gauge their rough proportion to one another (i.e., strong admiration with a touch of jealousy). Five or more successes allow the Abyssal to sense all emotions her target currently feels, as well as give her a rough sense of the target's permanent Willpower and Virtue allocation (weak, unremarkable, strong, overpowering, etc.). Regardless of the successes rolled, this Charm does not provide context. Even if a deathknight notices coiling tendrils of hatred in a target's aura, she doesn't automatically know who she hates or why he hates.

name: Soaring Raptor Prana
summary: Caps the Day Caste Athletics tree; grants the Abyssal true flight after a full turn of concentration, at an upkeep of 2 motes per turn.
description: Where he could only glide with Autumn Leaf's Descent, an Abyssal with this Charm can truly — if briefly — fly. The character must spend a full turn in concentration as he floods his being with Essence. At the end of the turn, he is borne aloft on spectral winds and may subsequently fly wherever he wishes. These winds cause capes and cloaks to billow and flutter, giving the illusion of wings if the character is so attired. Characters may keep this Charm active as long as they continue to spend 2 motes of Essence each turn, but they will stop flying normally once they stop paying this reflexive upkeep. All Essence spent on Soaring Raptor Prana is completely committed until the character ceases flying. While propelled by this Charm, Exalts move (Dexterity x 9) yards per turn and may attack other aerial combatants normally or assault targets on the ground using ranged weapons. Alternately, they can swoop and strike as they pass. Unless they are swooping, flying characters can only be attacked by ranged weapons, by other flying/leaping characters, or on the initiative count when they strike a ground-based target in close combat. As usual, characters rolling higher than the Abyssal can delay their initiative to strike at the necessary moment. Due to the Exalt's speed, individuals other than his target strike him at a -3 dice penalty unless wielding a long weapon, such as a spear, in which case the penalty drops to -1. The Exalt's target can attack him normally without penalty so long as the Exalt is attacking in return.
prerequisiteText: Autumn Leaf's Descent; Falling Scythe Attack

name: Striking Snake Grab
summary: Closes out the Day Caste Larceny tree; lets the Abyssal instantly steal a small, unsecured object in his line of sight.
description: The Abyssal extends his hand in a lightning-fast clutching gesture, reaching out with his Essence to steal an object in his direct line of sight. The targeted object flickers and rematerializes from Elsewhere in the character's grasp. This Charm can only grab objects small enough to comfortably hold with one hand and may not take possession of an object that is part of a sentient being's grasp. Possessions on a person's body can be grabbed but not if they are securely fastened (a money pouch could be grabbed but not the belt it is affixed to, for example). Ultimately, the Storyteller retains final say on what can or cannot be taken with this Charm.
